prompt: Some people believe that individual efforts to live more sustainably achieve nothing while governments fail to regulate polluting industries. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Nowadays, the climate change is one of the biggest problem in the world. Some people think that when a person try to live in a green way, it is useless, because the government do not control the big companies. I agree with this opinion in some way, but I also think that individual is still important.

Firstly, it is true that the industry produce much more pollution than the normal people. For example, if I recycle my plastic bottles every day, this is only a very small amount comparing to a factory which is burning coal for many years. So the government should make strong laws for these companies, because only the government have this power. Without the law, the companies will never change, because they only think about the profit.

Secondly, however, I do not think that the individual actions are completely useless. If many people change their habit, the companies will see that the customers want the green products, and they will change also. Moreover, when people live in a green way, they will vote for the politicians who care about the environment. Also, the children see their parents doing this and they will learn the good habit from them, so the next generation will be more responsible. This is also important for the future of our planet.

In conclusion, I agree that the government regulation is the most important thing for solving this problem, but I do not agree that the individual efforts are useless, because they can also push the companies and the politicians in the good direction.
title: Individual action against climate regulation
